chapter_theme: A single song at Periyamadam (பெரியமடம்), a monastery: the poet confesses learning the arts of love from courtesans and wasting the body and its days, and asks for initiation to stand on the path; the praise is a litany of 'potri' that names Murugan the lord of the tower at Arunai and 'the father called Arunagirinathar'.

823.reading: The poet confesses that in the hands of quarrel-eyed women he learned the false, thieving books of love, bathed and perfumed himself with civet, musk and tulasi for desire of their breasts, made a bed known to the whole land, waited at the window, thought all wealth and rule had come true, ran melting and stammered in embrace, and so wasted this illusory body and precious days; he asks that Murugan give initiation to one without sense, so he may stand on the path. The praise is a chain of 'hail': to the master exalted by boundless Tamil, to the one fond of the tower of Arunai, to the rider of the peacock, the six-faced lord called the father, the dancer who runs through all shrines, the father called Arunagirinathar, the vel against the Asuras, the guru of Siva who holds the skull, Valli's embrace, and the lord of the joy of Periyamadam, gained by the penance of a Dakshinamurthy unknown to Brahma, a lion to other sects.
823.nuance: நெறி நிற்க நீ தீக்ஷை தரவேணும்: the plea is for formal initiation (தீக்ஷை), fitting a monastery shrine. அருணை நகர் கோபுர விருப்பனே and அருணகிரி நாத எனும் அப்பனே: Murugan is called by the name of the Lord of Arunai, which is also the poet's own name, and placed at Tiruvannamalai's tower. Whether the Dakshinamurthy of the last lines is Siva as the silent teacher or the ascetic who founded the madam, a 'lion to other sects' (பரசமய கோளரி), the text does not settle.

links.note: 823 confesses wasting the illusory body and precious days on women and asks Murugan to give initiation so he may stand on the path (நெறி நிற்க நீ தீக்ஷை தரவேணும்). Tirumanthiram 1845 names what initiation does: samaya initiation purifies mala and one's own acting ceases (சமைய மலசுத்தி தன்செயல் அற்றிடும்), followed by mantra and kala purification. The Tirumanthiram gives the content of the rite the song asks for as its cure.
